newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank's Welteke - mark depreciation should stop.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank's Welteke - mark depreciation should stop.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said on Monday the mark's depreciation should not continue and that the unit's rise seen in 1995 had now been fully corrected.
Welteke also said the possibility of a U.S. interest rate increase had reduced the Bundesbank's scope to reduce German interest rates.

"The mark appreciation of 1995 has now been corrected, the exchange rate changes must not continue," Welteke told reporters before a conference on European monetary union in the northern German town of Kiel.

Asked if the prospect of a U.S. rate increase had narrowed the Bundesbank's scope for a rate decrease in Germany, Welteke said "the scope to conduct an interest rate reduction has lessened as a result of that."

He added, "the development of M3 money supply, of exchange rates and the current inflation data do not speak in favour of an interest rate change downwards. The unemployment situation as well as the economic situation do not speak in favour of a change in the other direction. The Bundesbank has fulfilled its task."

Asked if he saw a danger that the mark's recent depreciation would fuel upward price pressures in Germany, Welteke said "at the moment, with these exchange rates, I see no danger for an increase in the inflationary trend, but import prices have risen."
Welteke also said a further rise in the dollar against the mark is no "no longer desirable."
